affected_system: waste collection, recycling, street cleaning, illegal-dumping, and sanitation response
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of sanitation crews, vehicles, and prevention resources
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for sanitation crews, vehicles, and prevention resources

assumptions: Requests, route events, tonnage, inspections, dumping evidence, contamination, and completion remain distinct.
Waste generation and service demand are measured or modeled with declared coverage.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for sanitation crews, vehicles, and prevention resources.

constraints.description: The sanitation, waste, and street cleanliness allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: sanitation commissioner and waste operations chief
decision_question: How should crews, vehicles, inspectors, containers, and outreach be distributed across service areas?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The sanitation, waste, and street cleanliness allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.decision_object: sanitation crews, vehicles, and prevention resources
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for sanitation crews, vehicles, and prevention resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.primary_outcome: priority sanitation workload without assigned capacity

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting sanitation crews, vehicles, and prevention resources, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: priority sanitation workload without assigned capacity
distributional gap in priority sanitation workload without assigned capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report assigned crews or vehicles as completed collection, cleaning, or prevention.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for sanitation crews, vehicles, and prevention resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate sanitation crews, fleet, and prevention capacity
transportability_risks: Collection systems, housing form, waste law, contracts, markets, and reporting behavior differ.
Request labels and tonnage do not fully capture cleanliness or illegal dumping.
